description:
Fridays are fun! The weekend is here, school is out, work is done (for some of us), and it’s a time to sit back, relax, and enjoy ourselves.  T.G.I.F !    You all know what that means... CARTOON FRIDAY!

Luckily, learning English through cartoons and jokes is FUN! To understand, we must know the vocabulary being used, and the ‘hidden’ message behind the wordplay and puns. Understanding this shows a true level of English comprehension. So, go ahead and start having fun. Look through the cartoons. Each cartoon has a caption that you can answer in the comment section below, I'd also like to know, which cartoon is your favorite and why?

Happy learning, studying, and connecting! <3

*to comment, click the comment bubble to the right of the post's title*

description:
Okay. You've got the grammar textbooks, dictionaries, and translators. In the classroom, you are a superstar. So why is it so difficult to sometimes understand what natives are saying in the "real world?" What is the difference between being an English language learner who sounds like a learner, and one who sounds more like a native? The answer to both of those questions: IDIOMS. According to Merriam-Webster Learner's Dictionary (the best ESL dictionary, ever!) an idiom is:  1 : an expression that cannot be understood from the meanings of its separate words but that has a separate meaning of its own.   2 :  a form of a language that is spoken in a particular area and that uses some of its own words, grammar, and pronunciations.    3 : a style or form of expression that is characteristic of a particular person, type of art, etc. [count]

In other words, it's language that's difficult to learn in a book, with no context, extremely useful and common in any English speaking country, and most importantly, a way to express YOU. So, how should you learn? As there are thousands (and thousands) of idioms out there, I recommend learning them by common theme. The great thing is that idioms can be categorized in so many ways. Find something that interests you, and do a search:  _____(interest) idioms and voilà, there you have it.

Or, leave it to me. Learn English idioms online with English Outside the Box.  In the comment section of each new weekly post, I encourage you to write a relevant story where you can try and use these new idioms, because without application, the learning process can be very difficult.   Happy learning! <3

*to comment, click the comment bubble to the right of the post's title.*

description:
Being fluent in English is all about having the right words to say, at the right time. How can you expand your vocabulary? 
You can start right here, with "Words of the Weekend." Two new useful words will be featured on my Instagram account, and listed here. The best way to learn these new words, is trying to utilize them in your daily conversations. So, try and write a sentence using these new words in the comment section. To write, click the comment bubble to the right of the post's title.

Instagram: http://statigr.am/jenesl760
